chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked him about a broken sword that is sold for dirhams. He said: 'If its silver content is less than the coinage (value), there is no harm; but if it is more, it is not suitable.'

key_terms.النَّقْدِ: the coinage/money (specifically silver dirhams in this context)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm (it is permissible)
key_terms.فَلَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not suitable (invalid or problematic)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a silver sword for silver coins if the metal value differs from the coin value?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the application of *riba al-fadl* (excess in exchange) to mixed-metal items like swords, distinguishing between the intrinsic silver value and the currency's face value. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that when exchanging silver for silver, the transaction is valid only if the weight/value of the commodity does not exceed that of the currency, preventing hidden usury in commercial transactions.
